- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply in next 3–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving >2% from 30d mean, model often fails to revert; adjust forecast toward historical mean within 7–10 days.
- For 30d horizon, model overfits short-term momentum; reduce forecast sensitivity to recent 5-day moves if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 values, model tends to overreact; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85–0.95) to forecast if sentiment is “strongly bullish”.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms bullishness.
